t: In planning for the use or development of water and land resources, all Federal agencies shall giro consideration to estuaries and their natural resources, and their importance for commercial and industrial developments, and all project plans and reports affecting such estuaries and resources submitted to the Congress shall contain a discussion by the Secretary of the Interior of such estuaries and such resources and the effects of the project on them and his recommendations thereon. The Secretary of the Interior shall make his recommendations within ninety days after receipt of such plans and reports.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the Secretary's "recommendations" and the review of project plans amount to consultation. Every actor here is inside the federal government: federal agencies, the Secretary of the Interior, and Congress. The section requires no outside party such as states, the public, or experts to be consulted or heard, so it is intra-government coordination and reporting to Congress, not participation.
fable.s: all project plans and reports affecting such estuaries and resources submitted to the Congress shall contain a discussion by the Secretary of the Interior of such estuaries and such resources and the effects of the project on them and his recommendations thereon

qwen_block.w: This section requires the Secretary of the Interior (a federal official) to provide a discussion and recommendations to Congress (a federal entity) regarding project plans. Both the actor providing the input and the recipient are inside the federal government. There is no requirement to consult with or coordinate with outside parties such as states, tribes, the public, or private entities before making a decision.
qwen_block.s: all project plans and reports affecting such estuaries and resources submitted to the Congress shall contain a discussion by the Secretary of the Interior of such estuaries and such resources and the effects of the project on them and his recommendations thereon.

opus.w: Under this section, federal agencies must consider estuaries, and project reports sent to Congress must include a discussion and recommendations from the Secretary of the Interior. Every actor here is federal: the agencies, a cabinet secretary and Congress. Coordination between agencies and reports to Congress are both excluded from participation. No outside party is consulted or given a role, so the procedural wording does not make this participation.
opus.s: all project plans and reports affecting such estuaries and resources submitted to the Congress shall contain a discussion by the Secretary of the Interior of such estuaries and such resources and the effects of the project on them and his recommendations thereon.
opus.b: The tempting reading is that this is participation because one actor's "recommendations" must be included in project plans before they go to Congress. That fails because everyone involved is inside the federal government: the federal agencies, the Secretary of the Interior and Congress. No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public takes part.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the Secretary of the Interior to include a discussion in reports submitted to Congress. Congress is part of the federal government, so this is an intra-governmental reporting requirement. It does not require consultation or coordination with any party outside the federal government, such as states, tribes, or the public.
qwen_chat.s: all project plans and reports affecting such estuaries and resources submitted to the Congress shall contain a discussion by the Secretary of the Interior of such estuaries and such resources and the effects of the project on them and his recommendations thereon.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the Secretary of the Interior must discuss the effects of projects on estuaries, this involves coordination with outside entities or the public. However, the text only mandates that the Secretary include a discussion in reports submitted to Congress. Congress is inside the federal government, and the Secretary is a federal official. There is no requirement to consult with states, tribes, the public, or other non-federal entities. The interaction is purely intra-governmental (agency to Congress).
